blogs.title: From Tokens to Whole Sentences: Why Sequence‑Level Importance Ratios Matter in RL for LLMs
blogs.description: An accessible breakdown of the core insight behind GSPO – moving the importance‑sampling correction from individual tokens to entire sequences. The post explains the intuition, why token‑level ratios cause instability, and how sequence‑level clipping aligns with rewards, using simple analogies and visual illustrations.

blogs.title: Stabilizing Mixture‑of‑Experts (MoE) Models with GSPO – No More Routing Replay
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into the unique challenges of training sparse MoE language models with reinforcement learning. The article walks readers through the expert‑activation volatility problem, the previous workaround (Routing Replay), and how GSPO’s sequence‑level approach naturally resolves these issues, making MoE RL training simpler and more efficient.

blogs.title: How GSPO Boosts Training Efficiency: Less Token Clipping, More Learning
blogs.description: Explores the surprising empirical finding that GSPO clips a far higher fraction of tokens yet achieves better sample efficiency than GRPO. The blog uses charts and analogy to explain why sequence‑level clipping reduces gradient noise and leads to faster convergence.

blogs.title: Simplifying RL Infrastructure: Using Inference‑Engine Likelihoods Directly with GSPO
blogs.description: Shows how GSPO’s reliance on sequence‑level likelihoods tolerates precision differences between training and inference engines. Readers learn practical benefits for distributed training pipelines, partial rollouts, and multi‑turn RL scenarios.

blogs.title: GSPO vs. GRPO: A Step‑by‑Step Comparison of Objectives, Gradients, and Real‑World Performance
blogs.description: Breaks down the mathematical differences between GRPO and the new GSPO algorithm in plain language. Includes side‑by‑side gradient illustrations, pseudocode snippets, and real benchmark results from Qwen3 models to illustrate the performance gap.
